study type: Experimental animal study (randomized controlled trial in rats)
cohort: Thirty-six pregnant rats were randomized into three groups: control, hyperthermia at 40°C, and hyperthermia at 41°C.
finding: The hyperthermia-induced IUGR model demonstrated a significant inverse correlation between fetal weight and maternal body temperature, with higher maternal temperatures leading to lower fetal weights and associated placental damage and vascular modifications.
birth_weight: Fetal weight was significantly higher in the control group compared to hyperthermia groups (40°C and 41°C), and significantly lower in the 41°C group compared to the 40°C group.
gest_age: Interventions and measurements were performed at gestational days (GD) 18, 19, and 20.
